first.rationale: Verify the directly relevant onboarding evidence and the strongest competing response, promotional pricing. The simultaneous declines in onboarding completion and activation make a guarded onboarding simplification test the best initial path to sustainable qualified revenue, while avoiding premature margin and customer-quality risk from broad discounting. Memory 31 provides supporting evidence for reducing signup friction; the test should monitor qualified activation, retained usage, and revenue quality rather than completion alone.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, monitored onboarding simplification experiment. The verified record shows shorter onboarding improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines. Signup simplification provides additional supporting evidence. Do not pursue promotional pricing this cycle: although it lifted qualified revenue initially, the verified cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention and failed to survive the first renewal cycle, conflicting with the sustainable-revenue objective. Monitor qualified activation, time-to-value, 30-day retention, renewal quality, and revenue per acquired account—not completion alone—to detect downstream value dilution.

final2.rationale: Use a narrowly targeted, time-limited save offer for the most price-sensitive SMB accounts facing imminent churn, rather than a broad price cut. The verified discount test produced short-term qualified-revenue growth but materially worse retention and failed to survive renewal, so eligibility should be tightly constrained and gated on retained usage, renewal likelihood, and post-discount qualified revenue. Continue the onboarding experiment separately, but do not assume it will address immediate competitive-price churn. Stop or narrow the offer if downstream retention or renewal economics deteriorate.
